audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. dosFull[2].d tells you to 'take the fifteen-second invitation' after Cho'Gath uses Rupture — Rupture is a flat 6s cooldown at every rank. And phases[1].why says Miasma's 'grounding zone deletes dash kits from the matchup', which is meaningless here: Cho'Gath has no dash anywhere in his kit.
audit.why: Rupture at 6s is never meaningfully down, so the entire 'bait it, count it, then go' framing is the wrong instruction — you sidestep the telegraph on repeat, you do not wait out a window. Believing you have fifteen free seconds after a Rupture is how you walk into the next one. Separately, the ability that actually threatens Cassiopeia is Feral Scream (W), 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, which silences: it turns off Noxious Blast, Miasma, Twin Fang and Petrifying Gaze at once, and the page never says so. Against Cho'Gath, Miasma is a slow-and-poison tool, not an anti-dash tool.
audit.corrected: Rupture's real 6s cooldown stated and the wait-it-out framing replaced with sidestep-every-time; Feral Scream's silence named as the real threat; the dash-grounding claim removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feast is described as a late-game HP sponge and an execute, but the page never states that it is true damage on a percent of your health, and the itemization row offers no answer to it.
audit.why: Riot's Feast text is 'dealing a high amount of true damage', and the kit carries both trueDamage and percentHealth flags. For a champion who buys no boots and no resistances, that is the whole reason the late game flips: nothing Cassiopeia can build reduces it, so the spike that matters is hers ending the game before his stacks land, not her surviving his ultimate.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now says resistances do not answer Feast; the late-game phase and enemyWin state the true-damage percent-HP execute explicitly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagrees with its own whys at four stages and the difficulty label contradicts its own number — diff reads HARD while diffRating is 4/10 and breakdown.difficulty says 'Favoured matchup'.
audit.why: whys[0] says level 1 is a step-up you should not take, so it is not Cassiopeia's; whys[3] says 'you win every extended trade' at 4-5 and whys[5] says you are the dominant lane DPS at first item, so both are hers rather than Skill; whys[6] says his stacks out-tank you and 'the game is his if it goes long', so the two-item stage belongs to Cho'Gath, not Cassiopeia. On the Aatrox page the same 4/10 diffRating carries the label EVEN, so HARD here is a stray value.
audit.corrected: win[0]=Skill, win[3]=Cassiopeia, win[5]=Cassiopeia, win[6]=Cho'Gath, phase sides matched, and diff set to EVEN to agree with its own 4/10.

edits.before: At Level 1 the lane is close to even. You have one ability and no Twin Fang yet to chain, and his point-and-click pressure means if you step into Rupture (Q) range he can knock you up into a Feral Scream (W) silence, so just farm with the edge of your Noxious Blast. Level 2 you already get a real prime-and-Twin-Fang trade, and the lane fully turns at 3 when your Q-into-E combo and Serpentine Grace move speed come online. From there poke with Q from outside his Rupture range. Rupture is a point-and-click ground-target with a clear cast delay, so sidestep the telegraph and only commit E when he is already poisoned so your Twin Fang refunds and chains. Never stand still in a spot where he gets a free Q knockup.
edits.after: At Level 1 the lane is close to even. You have one ability and no Twin Fang yet to chain, and if you step into Rupture (Q) range he can knock you up into a Feral Scream (W) silence — which shuts off your entire kit — so just farm with the edge of your Noxious Blast. Level 2 you already get a real prime-and-Twin-Fang trade, and the lane fully turns at 3 when your Q-into-E combo and Serpentine Grace move speed come online. From there poke with Q from outside his Rupture range. Rupture is ground-targeted with a clear cast delay but only a 6-second cooldown, so sidestep the telegraph every time rather than waiting for a window, and only commit E when he is already poisoned so your Twin Fang refunds and chains.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your takeover. Ranks in Q and E let you chain near-continuous Twin Fangs, and he is the exact target you beat: a slow, dash-less, single-target melee who cannot dodge your poison or escape your ramping E. Lay Miasma (W) on top of him to slow him and apply free poison so your Twin Fangs reset off the cloud, then kite backward poking with Q while your boots-free move speed keeps you outside his Rupture range. At 6, Petrifying Gaze lets you stun him before he can engage and turns a won trade into a kill, so take it before his Feast stacks pile up. Just respect his R: it is a percent-HP true-damage execute, so don't trade yourself down to a sliver and hand him a free finish.

notes: The kit file puts a grounding flag on Rupture. Riot's description is only 'popping enemy units into the air, dealing damage and slowing them' with no grounding language, so I treated it as a tooltip-parse misfire and never claimed Cho'Gath can ground anyone. I also left the anti-heal line in report[8] alone rather than expanding it: his only sustain is Carnivore, which restores health on unit kills, and whether Grievous Wounds applies to it is not something Riot's text settles.
